kind: author-authored source-bounded assessment, not automated discovery
knowledge_boundary: Citations and facts use only the 2015 packet; author already exposed to later outcomes. No blind or independent forecast claim.

facts.quote: 425 Grand Concourse corresponds to Block 2346, Lot 1, and comprises approximately 30,049 square feet
facts.interpretation: City-owned site, approximately 30,049 sf; BBL 2023460001 constructed from borough/block/lot, not surveyed area.

facts.quote: The Site is currently zoned C4-4.
facts.interpretation: As described in the RFP, existing zoning is C4-4, not the proposed C6-3.

facts.quote: Proposals should assume a C6-3 district.
facts.interpretation: Proposal assumption contingent on rezoning and disposition; not an entitlement clearance.

facts.quote: The Project will also require City Council and Mayoral approval.
facts.interpretation: HPD ULURP applicant; map change, disposition and UDAAP anticipated; environmental review also required.

facts.quote: may take at least one (1) year from commencement.
facts.interpretation: At least one year for HPD design approval and ULURP including certification; not total delivery time.

facts.quote: Proposals must have mixed-income, affordable housing units.
facts.interpretation: Required residential program; exact affordability schedule still to be designed.

facts.quote: minimum of 15% three-bedroom units and a maximum of 15% studio units.
facts.interpretation: Base unit mix rule, with Addendum 1 supportive-housing flexibility; not an unconditional final-building compliance test.

facts.quote: HPD is open to seeing more than 15% studio apartments if necessary to serve the special needs population identified.
facts.interpretation: Supportive-housing branch requires evidence; no generic exemption assumed.

facts.quote: in no case less than thirty (35) years.
facts.interpretation: Source has conflicting word and numeral. Request clarification; do not silently normalize to 30 or 35.

facts.quote: The Project should include ground-floor retail or a mix of retail and community facility use
facts.interpretation: Program direction/preference, not a named committed tenant. A detailed feasible use/operations plan is required.

facts.quote: must be incorporated into the interior design of the building to commemorate the former P.S. 31
facts.interpretation: Architectural elements must be reincorporated and transported by developer.

facts.quote: The Developer will be responsible for the improvement and maintenance of the pedestrian walkway
facts.interpretation: Walkway improvement and maintenance required; playground funding is a competitive preference, not assumed required rehabilitation.

facts.quote: any primary or secondary egress into the walkway is not permitted.
facts.interpretation: A door can be permitted but cannot supply required primary or secondary egress; architect must test circulation.

facts.quote: HPD does not have any additional information regarding the route of the train.
facts.interpretation: Subway route relative to site unresolved; conditional MTA coordination, not confirmed tunnel geometry.

facts.quote: HPD does not provide surveys for its RFP sites. This is the responsibility of the developer.
facts.interpretation: No supplied survey/borings confirmed by these answers; commission site-specific survey/geotechnical diligence.

facts.quote: We are aware that construction costs may be higher in taller structures
facts.interpretation: Density and construction cost interact; no assumed low-rise cost for maximized FAR.

facts.quote: This assessment has revealed no evidence of recognized environmental conditions in connection with the Site.
facts.interpretation: Phase I executive summary reports no REC and three HRECs; no warranty of clean ground or geotechnical suitability.

facts.quote: Only the report in its entirety should be relied upon
facts.interpretation: Executive summary restricts reliance and is not a substitute for full report.

facts.quote: The Developer will be solely responsible for any mitigation measures identified as a result of the CEQR review.
facts.interpretation: Budget studies and mitigation; do not convert no REC into an environmental clearance.

facts.quote: completing demolition of the exterior wall and bringing the Site fully to street level.
facts.interpretation: Developer residual demolition and grading obligation remains after City school demolition.

facts.quote: As-of-right 4% tax credits are not considered competitive.
facts.interpretation: Primary scenario excludes competitive government sources such as 9% LIHTC. 4% branch allowed, not committed.

facts.quote: Proposals that assume HDC bond financing (and subsidy financing, if applicable) must comply with all terms of the applicable HDC term sheet.
facts.interpretation: Separate bond-related debt, subsidies, tax-credit equity and developer equity; historical term sheets not recovered.

facts.quote: will pay a nominal disposition price of $1.00 per lot and will deliver an enforcement note and mortgage
facts.interpretation: Nominal cash land price does not erase enforcement note, financing conditions, taxes or mitigation.

facts.quote: at least seventy (70) residential units within the past seven years.
facts.interpretation: At least one applicant principal must meet the defined new-construction development experience; actual credentials unknown.

facts.quote: at least seventy (70) residential units in New York City within the past seven (7) years.
facts.interpretation: Comparable management requirement for principal or proposed managing agent; actual credentials unknown.

facts.quote: no later than 4:00 p.m. on Monday, September 28, 2015
facts.interpretation: Source cutoff September 28, 2015 16:00 America/New_York; last retained addendum September 4, no extension found in packet. Completeness of historical addendum set uncertified.

facts.quote: one (1) bound original, one (1) bound copy and one (1) flash drive
facts.interpretation: Physical and electronic submission; D-1, D-2 and K original-format Excel required.

facts.quote: they are in physically separate buildings.
facts.interpretation: Addendum 2 refines rental/homeownership mixing preference; do not treat Addendum 1 permissiveness as final instruction.

facts.quote: HPD will accept 2011 Overlays for the purposes of RFP review.
facts.interpretation: 2011 Green Communities overlay accepted for proposal review; not necessarily later construction requirements.

unknowns: Historical term-sheet versions and committed funding amounts
Survey, borings, subway geometry and engineering budget
Validated floor plans, allowable FAR by use and bulk envelope
Full Phase I report and current remediation scope
Final legal effective dates, closing documents and approvals
Complete historical addendum set and byte equivalence

conclusion.text: Run a bounded eligibility/finance/architect-engineer screen before committing to a proposal or claiming capacity. Project potential is supported; eligibility, feasibility and a funded capital stack are not established.

actions.question: Can this team meet the 70-unit/7-year thresholds?
actions.stop: Do not submit this team as eligible without evidence or an explicitly accepted structure.
actions.cost_time: unknown; documentary check likely limited but not measured

actions.question: Can an architect fit a viable mixed-use scheme under the proposed branch, with legal egress and costed high-rise construction?
actions.stop: Do not state a unit capacity until envelope, layouts and rule applicability are demonstrated.

actions.question: What surveys, tunnel protection and ground conditions change scope/cost?
actions.stop: Do not clear excavation risk from this document packet.

actions.question: Can lenders/investors and public programs support the proposed affordability and complete sources and uses?
actions.stop: Do not claim funded feasibility without eligible sources, amounts, terms, timing and commitments.

priority: Eligibility is a proposed inexpensive screen, not an empirically optimal order. Finance and engineering should be scoped together; actor budget and task costs absent.
completeness: 29 selected source claims, not an exhaustive RFP compliance inventory; appendices and spreadsheet formulas not independently audited.
